commands.name: apply_patch
commands.description: Preview or apply one typed graph patch as a single verified transaction: reversible mutation, one target compile, authoritative readback and optional explicit persistence. Two mutually exclusive shells share the envelope: the authoring shell (nodes/connections/pin_updates) and the migration shell, which publishes replace_entry (replaces a stale inherited implementation entry while preserving the downstream body), copy_subgraph / move_subgraph (bounded same-asset transfer of a selected node set between two graphs with explicit boundary mappings and both-graph recovery), prune_island (removes only the uniquely owned execution island of one entry, preserving every shared node and every retained-consumer link, with a published partition) and retire_entries (retires a selected set of inherited override events; the only migration allowed on compile-invalid Blueprints). Standalone command: it cannot run inside a rollback-enabled batch because an outer batch cannot undo its compile or save boundary. Limits: max_nodes=64, max_edges=256, max_client_id_length=32, max_request_size_bytes=65536, max_scanned_nodes=2048.

params.name: asset_path
params.description: Full asset path to the Blueprint asset; the patch request must name the same asset

params.name: target
params.description: Target locator: graph_ref with a canonical graph_guid (plus optional subgraph_path) or implementation with owner_class and function_name. Required by an authoring request and by replace_entry; copy_subgraph / move_subgraph, prune_island and retire_entries address their graphs through migration and must not carry target.

params.name: patch_id
params.description: Caller-generated UUID that deterministically derives the identity of every new node

params.name: expected_fingerprint
params.description: Stale-write guard copied from graph.get_authoring_context: graph_authoring_version 1 plus graph_authoring_hash, package_saved_hash, is_dirty, dirty_epoch and not_ready

params.name: nodes
params.description: Authoring shell only: nodes to create or select, each with client_id, node_class, optional params, tagged defaults and position. node_class accepts a canonical class path or a family identifier. Supported families: CallFunction, VariableGet, VariableSet, Self, DynamicCast, ConstructObject, Event. Required for an authoring request (migration absent) and absent or empty for a migration request.

params.name: connections
params.description: Authoring shell only: edges between planned client ids or existing node GUIDs: from and to each carry client_id, node_guid or entry, plus pin. Required for an authoring request and absent or empty for a migration request.

params.name: pin_updates
params.description: Authoring shell only: existing input pin defaults to rewrite, each with node_guid, pin and a tagged default. Absent or empty for a migration request.

params.name: migration
params.description: Migration shell selector, one operation per request. replace_entry: {"op":"replace_entry","source":{"graph_ref":{graph_guid,graph_kind?,subgraph_path?},"entry_node_guid":"<guid>"},"pin_map":[{"entry":"input"|"output","from_pin":"<stale pin>","to_pin":"<replacement pin>"}],"remove_shadowing_member":false}; it requires target.implementation. copy_subgraph / move_subgraph bound a same-asset transfer: {"op":"copy_subgraph"|"move_subgraph","source":{"graph_ref":{graph_guid,graph_kind?,subgraph_path?},"node_guids":["<guid>",...]},"destination":{"graph_ref":{...}},"boundary":[{"from":{"node_guid":"<selected source node>"},"to":{"node_guid":"<existing destination node>"}}]} with a pin per endpoint; every crossing edge of the selection needs exactly one boundary entry. prune_island removes the uniquely owned execution island of one entry: {"op":"prune_island","source":{"graph_ref":{graph_guid,graph_kind?,subgraph_path?},"entry_node_guid":"<event or function entry guid>"},"approved_node_guids":["<guid>",...]} where approved_node_guids is the caller's echo of the removable set the preview publishes (omit it to preview the partition, never send it empty); the preview also publishes shared, blocked and external_edges plus complete and scan counts, and the apply removes only links whose far endpoint is an approved deleted node. retire_entries: {"op":"retire_entries","source":{"graph_ref":{"graph_guid":"<ubergraph guid>"},"entry_node_guids":["<override event guid>",...]},"approved_node_guids":["<guid>",...]}; selected entries must be override-style UK2Node_Event nodes. Retirement is the only migration permitted when the target Blueprint is compile-invalid. Every shell refuses a non-empty nodes/connections/pin_updates array; the transfer, prune and retirement shells refuse 'target'.

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Strict JSON boolean (numeric or string values are refused, never coerced). Preview only, and never mutates, compiles or saves (default: true); an apply needs the expected_validation_hash returned by a preview

params.name: compile
params.description: Strict JSON boolean (never coerced). Compile the target once after a reversible apply (default: true)

params.name: save
params.description: Strict JSON boolean (never coerced). Persist the target package after verified readback (default: false); requires compile=true and a clean starting package

params.name: allow_noop
params.description: Strict JSON boolean (never coerced). Permit an explicit change-free patch instead of refusing it (default: false)

params.name: expected_validation_hash
params.description: validation_hash returned by a preview; required when dry_run is false

commands.name: adopt_scs_into_native
commands.description: Hand an SCS component of the Blueprint over to a component it inherits, with a dry_run plan and a fail-closed readback. A component of a native parent is a default subobject of the generated class CDO (route native_cdo); a component of a parent Blueprint's SCS is overridden through the InheritableComponentHandler (route ich). Copies the transform and properties that differ from the SCS template's archetype (instanced subobjects are duplicated), re-attaches the child SCS nodes, retargets every K2 variable node and component-bound event, and removes the SCS node on request (children promoted first). Refuses a missing or stale target (STALE_PRECONDITION: compile against the native parent first), a class that is not the target's class or a child of it (INVALID_FIELD), dependents that reference a renamed component (INVALID_OPERATION), a same-named SCS node unless remove_scs=true, and data loss (POTENTIAL_DATA_LOSS with required_acknowledgment: child_override:<blueprint>, property:<name>, instanced sub-object keys). A Blueprint in error is accepted only when every error is the duplicate-name collision of a mapped node. A compile error or readback mismatch restores the Blueprint.

commands.name: swap_scs_component_class
commands.description: Replace the component class of one of the Blueprint's SCS nodes in place, with a dry_run plan and a fail-closed readback. The replacement node takes over the variable name, VariableGuid, category, metadata, attach name, parent link, children and position among its siblings; properties of the shared native ancestry are kept, Blueprint component variables with a same-named, same-typed property on the new class move their value, instanced subobjects are duplicated, and everything else is dropped. Refuses a class that is not an actor component or not derived from the old class's native ancestor (INVALID_FIELD), child Blueprints that override the node through an InheritableComponentHandler record, dependents that reference the component and component-bound events the new class cannot serve (INVALID_OPERATION), and dropped variables with a non-default value until acknowledged_losses carries property:<name> (POTENTIAL_DATA_LOSS). A compile error or readback mismatch restores the Blueprint.

commands.name: replace_interface
commands.description: Move a Blueprint from an old interface to a new one in one guarded transaction (the issue-named thin entry over the graph.apply_patch replace_interface migration; both produce the same outcome for the same request). The graphs of the mapped function-style functions are adopted by a new description of the new interface so every body node keeps its GUID, each stale entry/terminator is replaced through the replace_entry path (pin_map is fail-closed, exactly as replace_entry), the old description and its unimplemented stubs are removed, and the Blueprint is compiled once with journaled recovery. It refuses an old interface that is not implemented, a new interface that is already implemented, an implemented old function missing from function_map, a to that is not a function of the new interface, an incomplete pin_map, an in-asset caller of the old interface (retarget it first) and a derived Blueprint that overrides a mapped function. dry_run is required: true returns the plan (functions, dropped_stubs, new_stubs), validation_hash and fingerprint_before and changes nothing; apply (false) requires expected_fingerprint (= fingerprint_before) and expected_validation_hash. An omitted patch_id is derived from the canonical request, so replaying an identical request is an unchanged no-op. Mutating: refused for an asset blocked after a failed recovery.

commands.name: export_dependency_graph
commands.description: Write a typed dependency graph (inherits, implements, calls_message, casts, spawns, creates_widget, widget_tree_child, listview_entry, level_placement, struct_use, enum_use, config) to a report file. Scheduled nodes are Blueprints, Worlds, user-defined structs and enums under the prefixes; targets outside the prefixes are external nodes. calls_message covers interface message nodes and typed calls whose function belongs to an interface class. level_placement means a World asset hard-depends on the Blueprint package, or an external actor package (One-File-Per-Actor / World Partition, /<Root>/__ExternalActors__/<map path>/...) of that World references the Blueprint. Self-referencing edges are dropped. Waves order strongly connected components by longest path using hard kinds by default; cycles lists components of more than one node. matched_assets reports the assets found under each path prefix and warnings names prefixes that matched nothing

params.name: path_prefixes
params.description: Mounted content folders whose assets form the graph (e.g. /Game/MyFeature)

params.name: out_path
params.description: Report file under the project Saved, Content or Config directory

params.name: edge_kinds
params.description: Edge kinds to derive (default all): inherits, implements, calls_message, casts, spawns, creates_widget, widget_tree_child, listview_entry, level_placement, struct_use, enum_use, config

params.name: ordering_kinds

commands.name: find_name_lookups
commands.description: Find by-name access to Blueprint members. C++ (project and project-plugin .h/.inl/.cpp sources, fixed roots; the UnrealCortex plugin is excluded): string-literal names passed to FindFunction, FindFunctionByName, FindFunctionChecked, FindPropertyByName, FindFProperty, FindUField, FindField, FindFieldChecked, CreateUFunction, BindUFunction, AddUFunction, RemoveUFunction, K2_SetTimer, K2_ClearTimer, K2_PauseTimer, K2_UnPauseTimer, K2_IsTimerActive, K2_IsTimerPaused, K2_TimerExists, K2_GetTimerElapsedTime, K2_GetTimerRemainingTime, and the first token of a literal CallFunctionByNameWithArguments command. Blueprint: K2_SetTimer, K2_SetTimerForNextTick and the K2_Clear/Pause/UnPause/IsActive/IsPaused/Exists/Elapsed/Remaining timer nodes with an unlinked literal FunctionName pin. Only literal names are detected: names held in variables or constants are not. Each hit lists the Blueprint functions, events, custom events, variables and component variables of that name under the prefixes; matched_names/unmatched_names split the looked-up names by whether any Blueprint member matched. scanned_files counts the source files actually read and unreadable_files lists the ones that could not be read; matched_assets reports the Blueprints found under each prefix and warnings names prefixes that matched nothing. With out_path the full result is written to that file and the response is a compact summary (counts plus the first 10 cpp, blueprint, matched and unmatched entries)

params.name: path_prefixes
params.description: Mounted content folders whose Blueprints are matched against (e.g. /Game/MyFeature)

params.name: symbols
params.description: Only report looked-up names in this list (case-insensitive)

params.name: out_path
params.description: Write the full result to this file (under Project Saved, Content or Config) and return only a compact summary; use it when the inline result would be too large

commands.name: find_duplicate_graphs
commands.description: Find duplicated logic across Blueprints. Graph units are function graphs, macro graphs and ubergraph event chains (an event node plus everything reachable from it). Units are normalised ignoring GUIDs, node names, positions, comments, reroute knots and disabled nodes; references to the owning Blueprint's own class read as 'self'. A node is described by class, member reference, typed pins of entry/result/event nodes, reflected scalar properties (object, enum, name, number) and non-default unlinked pin values; collapsed-graph contents are not expanded and function local variables (their types and defaults) are not compared. exact_groups share an identical normalised hash across two or more Blueprints (hash by iterative neighbourhood refinement, not a full isomorphism test, so rare regular structures may collide). similar_groups are same-named units of different Blueprints whose LOOSE node-descriptor multiset Jaccard ratio reaches similarity (loose: every reference to a Blueprint-generated class other than the Blueprint itself - member parents, cast targets, pin types, class pin defaults, widget classes - is replaced by its nearest native ancestor class name, and BP member references keep the member name only, so parallel sibling Blueprint classes compare equal; marked loose:true; exact groups stay strict), grouped as star clusters around a representative; members identical to each other collapse to one, and min_similarity/max_similarity are true over all member pairs (members linked only through the representative may be below the threshold). Widget trees: exact groups compare strict class+name multisets; similarity and widget_tree_similarity use (widget name, native ancestor class, parent widget name) tuples (kind widget_tree). blueprint_pairs counts each unit pair once and lists Blueprint pairs sharing exact or similar graphs, sorted by shared_graphs descending, with widget_tree_similarity. matched_assets reports the Blueprints found under each prefix and warnings names prefixes that matched nothing. Pairwise work is O(n^2) per same-name bucket, pruned by a size-ratio bound. With out_path the full result is written to that file and the response is a compact summary (counts plus the first 10 exact groups, similar groups and Blueprint pairs)

params.name: path_prefixes
params.description: Mounted content folders whose Blueprints are compared (e.g. /Game/MyFeature)

params.name: min_nodes
params.description: Smallest graph (or widget tree) size considered, integer greater than 0 (default 5)

params.name: similarity
params.description: Jaccard threshold for similar groups, greater than 0 and at most 1 (default 0.9)

params.name: out_path
params.description: Write the full result to this file (under Project Saved, Content or Config) and return only a compact summary; use it when the inline result would be too large

commands.name: find_interface_implementers
commands.description: List the Blueprints that implement an interface (a Blueprint Interface asset, a /Script/ class path, or a U/I class name). Implementers come from the Asset Registry ImplementedInterfaces tag, so only candidates are loaded; a Blueprint that inherits the interface from a parent Blueprint is listed with direct=false and via naming the declaring ancestor. Per interface function the implementation is function_graph (a graph of the interface description: graph_name, graph_guid, entry_node_guid, node_count), event (an event node: graph_guid, entry_node_guid, has_body) or none. With include_callers (default true) it also lists the call sites: callers are matched by the resolved owner of the member, never by name: UK2Node_Message (kind message), a UK2Node_CallFunction whose member parent is the interface (typed_call) and a UK2Node_DynamicCast to the interface (interface_cast); each site carries asset_path, graph_name, graph_guid, subgraph_path (dot-separated composite subgraphs), node_guid, node_class and function. Sites whose owner cannot be resolved but whose member name is an interface function are listed under unresolved_callers. A content interface narrows callers to the hard referencers of its package; a native interface has no content package, so every Blueprint under path_prefixes is loaded

params.name: interface
params.description: Blueprint Interface asset path, /Script/Module.Name, or interface class name (URipX or RipX; the C++ spelling IRipX is accepted)

params.name: path_prefixes
params.description: Mounted content folders whose Blueprints are searched (e.g. /Game/MyFeature)

params.name: include_callers
params.description: Also list the call and cast sites of the interface (default true)

params.name: function
params.description: Restrict the reported functions, and the message and typed-call sites, to one interface function (cast sites are not function-specific and stay)

params.name: out_path
params.description: Write the full result to this file (under Project Saved, Content or Config) and return only a compact summary; use it when the inline result would be too large

commands.name: find_type_usages
commands.description: Inventory where a user-defined struct (UDS) or enum (UDE) is used, classified, for a replacement by a native type; run against the native type afterwards it proves no residual use. The hard referencers of the type's package under path_prefixes are loaded (Blueprints, user-defined structs) or classified from the Asset Registry. Each usage has a category: variable (Blueprint member variable incl. array/set/map, with role type/map_key/map_value), local_variable and function_parameter (function entry/result and custom event user pins), pin (any other node pin of the type, incl. enum equality, for-each-enum and enumerator-name nodes; node_class, graph_guid, node_guid, pin), make_struct, break_struct, set_fields, struct_member (UK2Node_MakeStruct, BreakStruct, SetFieldsInStruct, StructMemberGet/Set), switch_enum, enum_literal, datatable_row_struct (from the RowStructure registry tag, the table is not loaded), data_asset (a UDataAsset instance that hard-references the type, or an instance of a Blueprint DataAsset class whose variables use it, with via_class), save_game (a Blueprint deriving from USaveGame that declares the type; .sav slot files are not scanned) and nested_struct (another user-defined struct with a member of the type). Assets that cannot be loaded are listed under load_failures and assets beyond the node budget under skipped_assets, never counted as free of the type; referencing assets of other classes are listed under other_referencers
